materials.provenance: Base colour re-baked (Cycles CPU, emission, selected-to-active) from the approved TRELLIS source mesh onto fresh smart-projected UVs (the 229k-triangle source atlas does not survive a 98% decimation); no ground-sheet removal and no rear-view projection, so the second row of crates, the back and the underside are as TRELLIS invented them. Tangent normals baked from the source geometry and whiteout-blended with colour relief (rope and sack folds survive mainly there); AO baked from the decimated geometry; roughness and metalness derived from colour inside declared regions (dark, unsaturated iron corner brackets; the saturated ochre hide on top); no tone lift. Base alpha opaque (never dyed). Artistic derivation, not measured PBR.

limitations: Single-view TRELLIS reconstruction from one approved concept: the far side, back and underside are TRELLIS's invention, with no rear-view painting projected onto them.
Roughness, metalness and ambient occlusion are derived from colour inside declared regions and Cycles bakes, not measured PBR or hand-painted masks.
One body mesh with its detail painted into a single 512 px base colour; there are no LODs, trim sheets or separate material layers.
Re-cooking is not guaranteed to be byte-reproducible: MikkTSpace tangents can round differently on a few vertices, and Blender's smart UV project can lay out an atlas differently between runs.
Decimated from 229k to 3,939 triangles: lashings, straps and sack folds survive mainly as baked normal relief, and the iron corner brackets are roughness and metalness regions, not geometry.
The concept shows one face of the load; the second row of crates, the back and the underside are TRELLIS's invention.
Fitted to the convoy's open bed (0.94 x 0.86 x 0.64 m, limited by the bed's length); it is hidden while the convoy carries no cargo, as the procedural crates were.
